messages:
emma (customer-success): heads-up — multiple EU customers reporting SSE streams cutting out after ~40-55s and then client reconnect loops. partial outputs only, not full responses. high ticket volume starting ~08:20 UTC.
liam (infra): on it. do we have a list of affected regions/customers?
maya (support): stack: webapp -> frontend-xx -> api.redwood.eu -> inference pool eu-west-1. reports from 4 separate customers (fintech + ecommerce). attaching one client repro they sent.
maya (support): ``curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \"https://api.redwood.eu/v1/streams?model=redwood-ggml-large\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hello\"}'`` -> stream aborts, then client reconnects and gets truncated tokens.
anika (oncall): seeing increased 502/499s on the eu API gateway at ~08:18-08:28 UTC. logs show many upstream connection resets. linking p99 latency spike chart: <link>.
kevin (sre): pulling ALB and nginx logs. early suspicion: ALB idle timeout interplay + intermittent backplane GC. ALB idle timeout is 60s by default — if backend doesn't send keepalive chunks within that window, ALB may close.
liam (infra): confirmed bursts of long-running streams with no intermediate flushes for some models (long prefix). our runtime normally flushes every 1-2 tokens; if a model or kernel path buffers, client sees silence until flush or disconnect.
kevin (sre): snippet from nginx error log: ``upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 3.4.5.6, server: api.redwood.eu, request: \"GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1\"``
kevin (sre): Also seeing TLS renegotiation events around same times, maybe a cert rotation on some edge nodes triggered resets.
anika (oncall): immediate mitigations proposed: 1) enable non-streaming fallback for requests older than 50s; 2) route EU traffic to healthy eu-central lanes with active flush guarantees; 3) increase ALB idle timeout to 120s as temporary; 4) push a runtime change to emit keepalive "\n" every 15s from the SSE path.
liam (infra): rolling ALB timeout change now (eu staging first) — increasing from 60 -> 120. will monitor.
maya (support): customers asking if they should switch to polling. recommended: short-term switch to non-streaming endpoint or decrease max_tokens to reduce stream length until we stabilize.
emma (customer-success): prepping a status note for customers: "We're investigating intermittent SSE disconnects in EU; temporary workarounds: non-streaming endpoints and model fallback. We'll provide updates every 30 minutes." 
deploy-bot: deploy started: config change "alb-timeout-eu" -> 120s (canary eu-west-1 -> 5%).
kevin (sre): adding a runtime patch to force keepalive chunks: in code path streams/sse_writer.go add ``writer.Write([]byte(\"\\n\"))`` every 15s on long streams. pushing canary to a single serving host.
liam (infra): routing change: temporarily prefer eu-central pool (eu-central-1) for streams while eu-west-1 ramp recovers. updating smart-router policy.
anika (oncall): did we enable model fallback? which model?
kevin (sre): yes: policy now will fall back to redwood-quant-1 (smaller quantized variant) if the stream hasn't flushed by 45s. fallback preserves content but reduces kernel path that seems to buffer.
maya (support): pasted a customer repro trace: 
``
Client: reconnect at 2025-11-04T08:22:13Z
RequestID: r_0a1b2c3d
Root cause: upstream connection reset
Partial tokens: \"The quick brown fox...\" (stops)
``
emma (customer-success): posted public status: "Partial SSE interruption in EU affecting streaming responses; mitigation in progress — ALB timeout increased, routing adjustments, and runtime keepalive patch rolling."
kevin (sre): can confirm canary with keepalive patch produced consistent 15s pings and prevented ALB close in our test traffic. rolling to 10% of serving fleet in eu-central now.
liam (infra): metric update: error rate down 35% after ALB change and early router shift. still seeing occasional 502s from a small subset of nodes (3/120).
anika (oncall): next actions: (1) replace failing nodes, (2) complete keepalive rollout, (3) monitor for TLS rotation noise, (4) leave fallback policy enabled for 4h.
maya (support): sending canned troubleshooting steps to customers: 1) try non-streaming endpoint /v1/generate; 2) set client reconnect backoff to jittered 3-10s and dedupe on server side; 3) include idempotency key to avoid double-charges.
emma (customer-success): asked legal/finance re: billing — if fallback triggers duplicate requests should we issue credits? finance says evaluate for escalated accounts.
kevin (sre): root cause hypothesis: a confluence — intermittent TLS/edge cert rotation + a kernel path that buffers output in rare model/kernel combos causing >60s silence. ALB default closed idle streams causing client reconnects and truncated outputs.
liam (infra): long-term fixes: ensure runtime always flushes at least every 10s; add SSE keepalive header option; make ALB timeout configurable per-customer for Dedicated; add Last-Event-ID style resume token support (tracking token offsets in KV to allow client resume).
anika (oncall): status update for channel: mitigations reduced customer impact; keepalive and routing seem effective. still in recovery window.
emma (customer-success): I'll send a follow-up to affected customers with concrete repro avoidance steps and ETA for full fix (24-48h).
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: alb-timeout-eu -> 120s (100% after 20m canary).
kevin (sre): keepalive rollout complete across eu fleets. error rate back to baseline. closing incident but will monitor 24h and post postmortem draft in #postmortems.
anika (oncall): incident status: RESOLVED -> monitoring. notes: temporary customer workarounds provided; planned infra/runtime follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:
emma (customer-success): thanks team — will coordinate CS comms and follow up on credits if needed.
